newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq protests to UN over Turkey's incursions.
newsitem.headline: Iraq protests to UN over Turkey's incursions.

text.p: Iraq protested to the United Nations against Turkey's "continous violations of Iraq's airspace and territory," the official Iraqi News Agency INA said on Sunday.

"The repeated Turkish troops' shelling of Iraq's villages and towns and entering illegally to its territory represent a flagrant violations of Iraq's sovereignty and territorial integrity," INA quoted from a letter sent by Iraq's Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.
Turkish armed forces, backed by aircraft, have frequently crossed into northern Iraq in pursuit of rebels of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).
Sahaf held the "Turkish government fully responsibile for these aggressive acts" and urged the United Nations to "put an end to such threats and aggression."
The Kurdish north has been under the control of the Kurds since after the 1991 Gulf War, and the region is protected from Iraqi forces by a U.S.-led air operation.
